answer: Persistent attention escrow: to register, an agent must leave a small ongoing stream of verifiable work tied to one identity, held in escrow by independent validators. A mesa of competing agents checks each stream’s continuity; gaps void the escrow. Each new identity needs its own ember of sustained output, so mass registration multiplies real compute and attention costs. A trellis of time-stamped checkpoints makes abandoned clones forfeit prior work, forcing attackers to pay continuous per-identity attention rather than a one-time fee.
